KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry & unseasonably mild weather continues today and 
Sat. Highs will be in the upper 50s to the middle 60s both days with 
readings a bit milder today. 

High pressure overhead will result in dry weather with unseasonably 
mild afternoons continuing today and Sat. Model cross sections 
indicate much of the high cloudiness will depart early this 
morning...resulting in plenty of sunshine. 925T on the order of 
+9C/+10C coupled with westerly flow should yield highs well into the 
60s today. Mid level temps a tad cooler on Sat...But still expect 
plenty of sunshine which should result in highs in the upper 50s to 
the lower 60s. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Widespread heavy rain later Sun into early Mon with 
1-3" possible. Low risk of flooding...but the progressive nature of 
the system may limit this potential. Splashover/Minor coastal flooding 
possible, but significant impacts not expected. Bulk of rain comes 
to an end Mon morning with a mild afternoon as temps rise into the 
60s. 

The models have come into much better agreement in coastal low 
pressure developing off the southeast U.S. coast early this weekend. 
Another piece of shortwave energy carves out a trough over the Great 
Lakes...which amplifies the upper level flow along the east coast. 
This will force this intensifying low pressure system up the coast. 
While there are still some differences in the models track...the 
latest operational runs have come more in line with a western track 
that the AI models have been advertising. This brings the potential 
for a swath of 1-3" of rain later Sun into early Mon across southern 
New England. There are even a few model solutions now that track the 
system so far west that those higher amounts are west of our region. 
Regardless...we do expect a period of widespread heavy rainfall in 
the later Sun to Mon timeframe. This system has southern stream 
origins and it will be loaded in moisture...so there is a low risk 
for flooding. However...thinking this potential is limited right now 
given the progressive nature of this system. In fact...much of the 
rain may be over by early-mid morning Mon! So worst of the rain will 
occur Sun night and highs Mon may reach into the 60s. 

As for winds...while the guidance has shifted westward with the 
track the intensity is not as strong as what some solutions were 
indicating yesterday. So while it may be quite breezy on the coast 
with 25-40 mph gusts...thinking most areas remain below any wind 
headline criteria. And given the limited wind risk...thinking that 
any coastal flooding/splashover during Monday/s high tide should be 
rather minor with a limited impact. Nonetheless...may see some 
typical brief nuisance coastal flooding in the typically vulnerable 
spots given high astro tides. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Dry & much colder weather follows Tue into Wed with 
highs in the 40s. Lows Tue night mainly in the upper teens & 20s. 

Behind this departing coastal storm...dry but much colder 
temperatures will work into southern New England. Significant cold 
advection should keep high temps mainly in the 40s Tue and Wed with 
perhaps some of the high terrain remaining in the upper 30s. High 
pressure overhead will keep us dry too and setup Tue night to be an 
ideal night of radiational cooling. Lows Tue night will probably be 
mainly in the upper teens and 20s with even downtown Boston likely 
dropping into the lower 30s. 

KEY MESSAGE 4...Another storm system will bring the potential for 
more rain to the region sometime Wed night into Thanksgiving. Ptype 
appears to be mainly rain...but there is a low risk for a bit of 
snow/ice at the onset across the interior. 

Much of the latest long range guidance indicates that another 
moisture loaded piece of southern stream energy may impact our 
region sometime Wed night into Thanksgiving. Ptype would favor 
mainly rain...But antecedent airmass may be just cold enough for the 
low risk for a bit of snow/ice at the onset across the interior. 
Certainly something to watch give Holiday Travel...But overall this 
mainly looks like a rain event.
